Hi Sarah,

Thanks again for the time today — really productive call. Below is a concise recap and confirmation of the pain points, goals, and next steps we discussed so we're all aligned.

Recap / Pain points:
- Current user-facing generation p95 latency is inconsistent (spikes during peak) and is impacting conversion.
- Acme needs predictable tail latency for interactive features (search-assist and chat).
- Workload has mixed short prompts (<=128 tokens) and occasional long-form generation (up to ~512 tokens).

Goals / SLOs discussed:
- Target: P95 generation latency <= 150ms for 128-token median requests (interactive flows).
- Target: P95 <= 300ms for 512-token requests under normal production load.
- Sustained throughput target: ~300 req/s (production), with burst capacity up to 1k req/s for seasonal spikes.
- Availability/SLA: 99.9% for the inference layer with graceful degradation to smaller model variant if necessary.

Model & topology notes from the call:
- Primary model family: ~13B family (you mentioned preference for open-vendor models).
- Strong preference for data isolation — considering Redwood Dedicated or Private (VPC) deployments.
- Networking constraints: private subnets and strict egress requirements (you said procurement will share a subnet diagram).

Immediate next steps (owner / ETA):
1) Acme to share traffic profiles (qps by hour), production sample traces, and the network diagram — Sarah to send by Tue 4/27. (Acme)
2) Redwood to propose two deployment topologies (Dedicated vs Private), with estimated latency/throughput and cost delta + recommended quantization and batching knobs. (Marissa / Rishi) — deliver by Thu 4/29.
3) Schedule 60–90m engineering deep dive to validate KV-cache, batching, and autoscaling behavior (proposed slots attached). (Marissa)

Attachments: acme-inference-requirements.xlsx (stub) — basic traffic profile template and SLO worksheet.

If that all looks right I'll schedule the deep dive and loop in Rishi (infra lead) and Dylan (solutions engineer) to walk through the runtime implications.

Thanks — talk soon,

Sarah — perfect, thanks for the network diagram and updated qps numbers. Looping Rishi and Dylan in so we can put together the topology options and cost deltas.

High-level deployment options (we'll expand these in the proposal):

Option A — Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools)
- Pros: predictable throughput, simpler setup, Redwood-managed control plane; fast time-to-production.
- Engineering implications: configure continuous batching with dynamic batch size cap and per-route latency SLOs; set KV prefix cache for hot prefixes to reduce p95; use a larger instance type for lower tail latency under concurrency.
- Expected performance: with 4x A100-equivalent GPUs (or cloud equivalent) + quantized 4-bit model, we expect to meet 150ms P95 for 128-token flows at ~400 req/s with proper batching and cache warmup.

Option B — Redwood Private (VPC)
- Pros: full network isolation, customer-managed VPC, KMS/HSM integrations for keys, best for compliance-sensitive customers.
- Engineering implications: additional work to validate egress rules, private subnets, and NAT/peering setup; may need a small dedicated autoscaling buffer to handle bursts; suggests colocating KV cache on same VPC when possible for lowest latencies.

Performance levers and recommendations:
- Model quantization to 4-bit where acceptable for quality-cost tradeoffs (Rishi to run initial eval).
- Dynamic batching settings: target small base batch for interactive flows (<=8) with a fast timeout; larger batches for backend jobs to improve throughput.
- Prefix/KV caching: cache common prompts/initial tokens to shave p95 on repeat queries.
- Graceful fallback: route to smaller model variant in overload scenarios to maintain latency SLOs.

Next steps:
- Rishi: can you run a quick eval on 13B => 4-bit quantized latency profile and include ballpark cost delta for Dedicated vs Private? (ETA: Thu 4/29)
- Dylan: please draft a one-pager that translates deployment options into procurement language (order-of-magnitude monthly cost, commit assumptions).
- Marissa: I'll schedule a 90m deep-dive for Mon 5/3 or Wed 5/5 — propose times once you confirm availability.

Attachment: redwood-deployment-options.pdf (summary + topo sketches).

Thanks all — looking forward to the deep dive.

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
